cards.typed_words:
B C D F G H J K L M N P R S T V W Y Z
She finds a bottle of pills and she holds them in her hand,
My whole world is falling down and noone understands.
There's only one way to solve my problems thats for me to go away,
When I'm in my grave I can't hear everyone say:
"She had the whole world in her hand but she only let us down,
Now she's gone too far away and it's only six feet under ground [crossed out: feet down]"
What could make her think that we didn't love her so,
What could make her think there was no place left to go?
I'm sorry mom - I'm sorry dad,
I hoped that this would make you glad.
I couldn't bare to see your face,
When you thought your love's a waste.
I didn't want to hurt you nor give you any pain,
I just imagined my loss would be your gain.
That would pass just like the moon with just a hug and hiss.
This is your one mistake that'll never be undone,
We used to have two children we're left with just a son
Everybody stumbles when they learn to walk,
And everybody mumbles when they learn to talk,
One thing that we've learned is to give it our best shot,
We prayed that you'd be strong but you never really fought.
Did you ever listen to anything you'd been taught?
When you swim against the tide you give it all you got
With your expectations so high you nailed me

whenever I shift to a higher gear I cant always

the wall?

Why did you say nothing? We should have known it all,
If you would've said something we would have been more kind.
Oh what have I done? This shouldn't be my fate,
I've only made one mistake and no [...cut for the check]

cards.name_on_card: Ode to Jason
cards.item_type: POEM · IN POEMS BY TOM · FULL POEM
cards.summary: loose leaf, blue ink, numbered 8 in cards
cards.typed_words:
This is a story about a boy who's dog ran away,
While during a snow storm he went out to play.
The dog made it home but the boy became lost,
He set out to find a loved one, no matter what the cost.
When you're a fourth grader finding a dog is no easy task,
Should you risk your life for a pet? It depends on who you ask.
The fact that Jason said yes should come as no surprise,
He loved that dog to pieces you could see it in his eyes.
Little Jason was a hero so he set out through the snow,
It saddens my heart deeply to tell his tale of woe.
What a brave little soul right up until the end,
What a brave little soul to go search for his friend.
A bit of inspiration is what he left behind,
He listened to his heart, paid no attention to his mind.
And when he left our world with the situation oh so grim,
The last thought that filled his head is that the dog would do the same for him.
The saddest of it all, the reason why we cried,
If not for the heart of an angel he never would have died.
When you think of him in memory try to wipe away the tears,
Remember what he was wise beyond his years.

cards.name_on_card: WALKING ALONE
cards.item_type: POEM · IN POEMS BY TOM · FULL POEM
cards.summary: spiral, torn
cards.typed_words:
WALKING ALONE

Alone in the crowd
My solitary parade
Shame holds my hand
Surrounding faces start to fade
We walk in unison
Chained by despair
Footstep after footstep
Going nowhere
Never asking directions
At least out loud
We just keep walking
Blending back in the crowd
We fade into the darkness
Of self-induced pain
Finding our way
By tapping our cane
After wandering for hours
while searching for our guide
I decided to close my eyes
And look deep down inside
With severed handcuffs left behind
I may now travel all alone
For I found the errors of my ways
In thinking that walking with shame
Was better than walking alone

---

Reincarnation
Legs spread wide open
muscle contractions push me right out the door
Soaking wet and thrown into a cold world
Ready to start a new tour
Groggy and crying
My eyes start to open
With my senses beginning to soar
I can't quite place it
Nor track or trace it
But something tells me I've been here before
There's no heaven or hell
As far as I can tell
Only new shapes and sizes
These different disguises
I've been a rich man, a poor man
A black man, a woman
A cat, a flea
A dog, a tree
All over the world
And every century
I've faught to supress
And I've faught to free

---

If I was a carpenter and you were a lady
What the hell?
I am a carpenter and you are a
bitch!
I build the caskets and you
dig the ditch
I lay 'em up and you lay 'em
down
Now ain't that a switch
Last one in line is the last in the
ground

I make my own gods and
worship my own idols
But at least I don't try
to pawn them off on you
Don't go knocking on doors
with my bible in hand
No bumper stickers about
Jesus - you know it's true
I worship my ears when
you talk on
I worship the ground that
you walk on
I worship your long blonde
hair
And your eyes so blue

---

I'm in love w/ myself [...cut for the check]

cards.summary: Handwritten text on lined notebook paper, in good condition.
cards.typed_words:
It's time to wake up
    Awake from out of your spell
    Can you smell that there's something in the air
    So familiar that I know it all too well
    
    One must be careful
    Of the company they keep
    For you do not know what your mattress does
    While you are asleep
    
    There's a lobbyist sleeping in the lobby
    Because they moved the capitol up to the hill
    He's dreaming of his new hobby
    He looks like he's dreaming still
    
    The man which the lobbyist selected
    His ego is inflated but he doesn't care
    Has anyone noticed that the president we elected
    His head is filled with graying hairs
    
    The dam next to where we live
    Has suddenly sprung a leak
    It's leaking like a siv
    So it seems that the future looks bleek
    
    Old men who've already
    Lived a lifetime
    Still think they get better with age
    But sour grapes do not make a fine wine

  [read/page 2  -  shot 512]
  TITLE : [NONE]
  PAPER : notebook
  LINES : 21
  TEXT  :
    Our grandfathers are all CEO's
    While grand children watch music videos
    Losing touch with reality
    Both the past and the future are scaring me
    {struck: Either you have too}
    
    Either you have too much
    Or too little gained
    Ain't nothing changed
    It's the same old problems again
    
    It's time to wake up

    It seems that daddy works seven days a week
    Even though us kids have plenty to eat
    Mommy teaches us and cooks and cleans
    And tells us to be nice when we are mean

cards.name_on_card: THE LIGHT
cards.item_type: POEM · IN POEMS BY TOM · FULL POEM
cards.summary: TYPED/PRINTED  -  flag for Tom, not handwritten
cards.typed_words:
THE LIGHT

My world is empty
As strangers pass I imagine myself endeared in their eye
They never stop, just go about their daily routine
Never wondering what an unknown figure could ever do for them
Perhaps make every dream come true, perhaps give them the sun and place it in
their hands
They walk by and their lives are changed forever, unknown to them
I could have been their everything
My life remains the same, alone
I am willing to love
Yet they never stop, just go about their daily routine
Sometimes I try to be noticed, I shout and wave my hands and make promises I
wholly intend to keep
But they do not stop, not for me
Desperate, I keep on searching
Filling my void with whatever I find to make the day pass
Night falls and covers my weeping eyes and wet cheeks
Despair fills my heart as darkness fills the air
Alone and in the dark my eyes catch sight of a distant light
So far in the distance and so high atop the sky
Seemingly a kin to the mountains it is so unreachable
Yet I must try
What have I to lose except the pain of tears?
With every step closer my sorrow is lifted
I walk long miles yet my legs do not feel heavy
My heart begins racing as the light does not fade as I get closer
So many times before my dreams crushed right before my eyes
Maybe once I will succeed, to reach the top
After an eternity of traveling I reach the summit
The light, once distant and small, encompasses me
I stand before it, anxious to touch it
I extend my hand in friendly greeting
The light enters my fingertip and explodes into my body
A body once cold regains warmth
Each sense more exited than the next
All pain ever felt before is exiled back to where it came
My spirit returns and I feel alive
The light I now hold within guides me
Through darkness
Through worry
Now as I have found the light [...cut for the check]

Burning the candle at both ends
Usually causes a fire

And no one's ever called me a liar

Life is so preciously short
That there's no time to waste
With so many piles of things to sort
They'll just get higher with haste

Slow and steady wins the race
In the end you'll realize your fate
If you plan your steps you can slow your pace
The best things come to those who wait

---

Everything that was once important
Has since made an about face turn
Ideals and values which I once wrote down so proud
The paper which they were written on has burned
[Caught a spark from some illumination
And I now watch them burn]

I once heard a wise man say
The only certainty in life is change
Opinions drift with each passing day
Nothing ever remains exactly the same

This good life I lead
Along with my love for you
I may find I don't need
And they could die too

The high path road that I walk on may crumble
I could find my self among the trash cans in an alley
The mountains I climbed could be a volcano and rumble
for fear of explosion I may hide in the valley

The very place where I learned how to climb
The waving road I travel could bend
blind

cards.name_on_card: We know the search is never easy
cards.item_type: POEM · IN POEMS BY TOM · FULL POEM
cards.summary: Lined notebook paper with handwritten text in black ink, displaying some crumpling and edge wear.
cards.typed_words:
(2)
We know the search is never easy
As you've found the bottom of your drink
though when your soul feels uneasy
Sometimes it makes you think

Would we be better
If we never considered ourselves brothers
Would our world be different
Had we never met each other

When in need of advice
Each other we seek
Yet the same hell goes on
Every week to week

Same old brand new day...
Same old story
We keep seeing ourselves
But the scenery gets boring

One hand washes the other
But the same goes when you're in the dirt
When all is said and gone you're still my brother
Even though we're the only ones getting hurt

---

(4)
We've both seen the worst that can happen
Even through what seemingly was the best of times
Celebrated many of nights
Written many a rhymes

It may in fact be hip to be square
Unfortunately the circle keeps its shape
We still got some years
But just how long will it take?

We never want to give up
On a family member taken in
But the question pops up
When you're surrounded by sin

False Gods I have never preached
By some higher power up there I truly beseech
Come to the aid of a couple fellows out of reach
Who's life's goal is goodness to teach

Giving to the takers
Take nothing from those who give
Do it long enough
You'll find your way to the bridge
